newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil hit by weak demand, negative sentiment.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil hit by weak demand, negative sentiment.

text.p: European fuel oil prices came under pressure from weak demand and bearish market sentiment on Wednesday, traders said.

Low sulphur swaps fell, dragging physical cracked down to $86/$87, though the only deal seen done was by a U.S. supplier with U.K. plant to a trader with a short need into Italy at a floating price heard to be high quotes plus $1.
That buyer was heard to be looking for top-up material.
Low sulphur barges also slipped to around $90 fob, with sellers under a little pressure. Swaps followed futures lower on the back of bearish U.S. stocks data.

High sulphur cargoes finally reacted to poor demand, dropping to around $79 fob, although one utility buyer put out an offer of $75 fob which the market was heard to have scorned, at least for the moment.
"High sulphur has begun to drift down, I'm hearing $79 or $78.50 is the best a seller will get at the moment," said one buyer.
High sulphur barges bucked the trend and held onto yesterday's values, although trade was only moderate.
Deals were done at $82.50 for prompt material and at $83 fob ARA for later delivery.
"Barges were a bit bubbly and then went dead," said one trader. "and again (high sulphur) fuel didn't follow Brent down." - Sean Maguire, London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
